name: Susac Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Susac Syndrome (Kleffner 2016)

criteria.description: Encephalopathy (cognitive/behavioral changes, confusion, memory loss, psychosis)
Branch retinal artery occlusion (BRAO) on fluorescein angiography
Corpus callosum lesions on MRI ('snowball' pattern, central callosal involvement)
Arteriolar wall hyperfluorescence on fluorescein angiography (even without frank BRAO)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Complete triad (encephalopathy + BRAO + SNHL) is diagnostic. Incomplete forms recognized with 2 of 3 features. Characteristic MRI findings (central corpus callosum 'snowball' lesions) are highly supportive. All three components may not appear simultaneously.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Often initially misdiagnosed as MS. Corpus callosum involvement in Susac is central/callosal body (not calloso-septal as in MS). Self-limited but may cause permanent damage if untreated. Anti-endothelial cell antibodies may be present.

searchTerms: increased muscle tone from brain nerves

laboratory: CSF: elevated protein, mild lymphocytic pleocytosis (50% of cases)
Anti-endothelial cell antibodies (research; not routinely available)
imaging: MRI brain: central corpus callosum 'snowball' lesions (highly characteristic); may also involve periventricular white matter, deep gray matter, cerebellum
MRI with contrast: leptomeningeal enhancement may be present
Fluorescein angiography: branch retinal artery occlusions (BRAO), arteriolar wall hyperfluorescence
OCT: inner retinal thinning from prior BRAOs
other: Audiometry: low-to-mid frequency sensorineural hearing loss (distinguishes from presbycusis)
Fluorescein angiography is critical (retinal changes may be subclinical)
Visual field testing: scotomata corresponding to BRAO

distinguishingFeatures: MS lesions are calloso-septal (undersurface), not central callosal
MS does not cause BRAO or hearing loss typically
MS has oligoclonal bands in CSF (Susac usually does not)
SLE has positive ANA, anti-dsDNA, multi-organ involvement
SLE CNS involvement differs in imaging pattern
Cogan syndrome has interstitial keratitis (not BRAO)
Cogan syndrome lacks encephalopathy/corpus callosum lesions

redFlags: Acute encephalopathy with personality change and confusion (may mimic psychiatric illness)
Rapidly progressive hearing loss (may be irreversible without early treatment)
Multiple BRAOs causing cumulative visual field loss
Severe corpus callosum involvement predicting poor neurological outcome
references: Kleffner I, et al. Diagnostic criteria for Susac syndrome. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry. 2016;87(12):1287-1295.
Susac JO. Susac's syndrome. AJNR Am J Neuroradiol. 2004;25(3):351-352.
Dorr J, et al. Characteristics of Susac syndrome: a review of all reported cases. Nat Rev Neurol. 2013;9(6):307-316.
